correctness.rationale: There are exactly 3^9 commutative unital tables in a fixed identity-bearing basis. The unital Waring-rank theorem reduces the invariant to a quadratic 3-space. A complete projective-quadric lemma over F3 proves rank <=5 iff the annihilator net contains a conic with at least five projective zeros. The pure-stdlib verifier enumerates all 364 projective quadrics, all 19683 tables, 432 unital basis changes, and separately all 1287 five-square subsets for each orbit representative. It proves exactly 288 sharp tables in two 144-member orbits, including division and associativity distinctions. No infinite generalization is inferred. The same exhaustive test proves rank six if and only if every nonzero multiplication operator is invertible.
